clue.text: Be fond of and look after

explanation.surface: Someone who loves a person and also looks after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard meanings of the phrasal verb: to feel affection for, and to tend or nurse.

clue.text: Constable is on to drug deal

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another is placed above it

parts.note: a constable is a police officer, informally a cop
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A policeman is wise to a drugs transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope with something is to deal with or manage it.

clue.text: A step up the ladder is called for

definitions.meaning: a crosspiece of a ladder you climb on

explanation.surface: A promotion is required.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a ladder's crossbar and the past participle of ring, meaning telephoned.

clue.text: Winter trip?

parts.note: a stumble, read also as the time once the American autumn has passed

explanation.surface: A holiday taken in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English fall is autumn, so when fall is over winter has come; trip means stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip and tumble is to lose your footing and fall down, and winter comes when autumn is past.

clue.text: In two ways they can produce fine sprays

definitions.text: In two ways they can produce fine sprays

parts.words: In two ways they can produce fine sprays
parts.note: sprays of blooms on a bush, and sprays of water from the perforated nozzle of a watering can

explanation.surface: Things able to produce a fine mist in two different ways.
explanation.definitionFit: These flowers grow in sprays, and the perforated nozzle on a watering can shares their name.

clue.text: The long version lacks nothing in measurement

definitions.text: The long version lacks nothing in measurement

parts.words: The long version lacks nothing in measurement
parts.note: the noun formed from the adjective long is itself a dimension, the extent from end to end

explanation.surface: An uncut film or text that is complete in every respect.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an extended edition of a film; the clue really points to the noun that the word long turns into, which is a measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance from end to end is a basic measurement, and it is the noun derived from the adjective long.

clue.text: Possibly run and see to make certain

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone should run to check something properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to guarantee or make sure, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bears out what she found in story?

definitions.text: Bears out what she found in story?

parts.words: Bears out what she found in story?
parts.note: reads as confirming a finding, but refers to the fairy-tale girl who visits the three bears' house while they are out

explanation.surface: Something that confirms what a woman discovered in a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale this girl enters the cottage of the three bears while they are away.

clue.text: They shouldn't be confused with the Household Brigade

definitions.text: They shouldn't be confused with the Household Brigade

parts.words: They shouldn't be confused with the Household Brigade
parts.note: the Household Brigade is the Guards regiments protecting the monarch; the wartime volunteers were a different kind of guard

explanation.surface: A warning not to mix up two military units.
explanation.walkthrough: The Household Brigade is the Guards regiments of the British Army; the volunteer force of the Second World War defending Britain had guards of another kind.
explanation.definitionFit: These were members of Britain's Second World War volunteer defence force, not the regular Guards regiments.

clue.text: Irregularity in sleep a disadvantage

indicators.note: irregularity suggests things out of their proper order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disturbed sleep puts a person at a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To disadvantage someone is to handicap or punish them, the verb sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Refuge a youth originally found in poor accommodation

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a slum is squalid, run-down housing

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A young person who has been living in squalor is given shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge or sanctuary is a place of safety, which is what this word means, as in political asylum.

clue.text: Hit and pinched

explanation.surface: Someone was struck and nipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to strike with a sweeping blow and, informally, to steal.

clue.text: Party MPs start cheering

parts.note: Members of Parliament collectively make up the House (of Commons)
warming means beginning to feel cheerful or enthusiastic, as in warming to an idea

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament begin to cheer in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The House is the House of Commons, the British parliament's elected chamber whose members are MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a party held to celebrate moving into a new home.

clue.text: If you do, you will be clearly out when turning ball goes to fielder

definitions.text: If you do, you will be clearly out

parts.note: in cricket a ball that turns off the pitch is said to break
cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket tip about a spinning delivery going to a fielder and a batsman being out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket terms dress up an idiom: breaking cover means leaving a hiding place, so you are out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: To break cover is to emerge from a hiding place, so you are plainly out in the open.

clue.text: Making uniform for a social occasion

explanation.surface: Smartening up a uniform for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both levelling things off and a night out socialising.

clue.text: A book to be critically examined, but not purchased

definitions.text: A book to be critically examined, but not purchased

parts.words: A book to be critically examined, but not purchased
parts.note: describes a free copy sent by a publisher to a critic for assessment

explanation.surface: A book someone must study closely without buying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishers send critics free advance copies so the book can be assessed in print.

clue.text: Many drinks may result in immobility

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
hock is German white wine, so hocks are drinks

explanation.surface: Too many drinks may leave someone unable to move.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is a British name for German white wine, especially Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedges placed against wheels hold a vehicle or aircraft in place, so they bring about immobility.

clue.text: A number returning with duck eggs

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

indicators.note: returning means the letters of the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number

explanation.surface: A figure comes back together with a duck's eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns A and V into VA, which follows O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural for egg cells, used in biology for eggs generally.

clue.text: Ape pulls out emu's tail

indicators.note: pulling something out of shape distorts it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word emu with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A monkey yanks feathers from a large bird's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulls out' rearranges EMUS TAIL; the S of the possessive counts here.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to imitate or mimic, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Two points on a beard

parts.note: W, west, is one compass point
N, north, is another compass point

explanation.surface: A beard with two sharp tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The bristly tip on an ear of barley or other grass is called its beard by botanists.

clue.text: Having conned Robin, indicated complicity

parts.note: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest
to wink is to signal a shared secret or collusion

explanation.surface: Someone tricked Robin and gave a knowing wink.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or trick someone is to have duped or fooled them.

clue.text: A lifeline?

parts.note: not a rope thrown to rescue someone but the line of work a person follows through life

explanation.surface: A rescue rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's chosen profession is the course their working life follows.

clue.text: Ratty makes sure a knot can be undone

indicators.note: a knot that is undone is untied, so these letters come apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irritable person checks that a knot can be untied.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable and bad-tempered, the same as quarrelsome and grumpy.

clue.text: Come up to stretch between bends

definitions.meaning: a straight length of river between two bends

explanation.surface: Someone arrives and stretches between exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: It means to arrive at, and also a straight section of river between bends.

clue.text: It's risky going out on this shoot

definitions.text: It's risky going out on this shoot

parts.words: It's risky going out on this shoot
parts.note: a shoot is a branch, and going out on one recalls the idiom for a risky exposed position

explanation.surface: A warning about the danger of attending a hunting day.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of a tree is a limb, and being out on one means being in a precarious position.

clue.text: Shoulder and stomach

definitions.meaning: to carry or take on a burden
to tolerate or put up with

explanation.surface: Two parts of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both to carry a load and to tolerate something unpleasant.

clue.text: Shrinking flower?

parts.note: points both to a small bloom and to the idiom for a shy, retiring person

explanation.surface: A flower that is getting smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is the idiom for a very shy person, and the violet is also a flower.

clue.text: Sad pair originally evicted, having erred here

definitions.text: Sad pair originally evicted, having erred here

indicators.note: to err is to stray or wander, so these letters have gone astray into a new order
originally means taking the first letter of the word evicted

explanation.surface: The unhappy couple, thrown out for their sin, once lived here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having erred' rearranges SAD PAIR with E, the first letter of 'evicted'. The whole clue is the story of Adam and Eve expelled from Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden, from which Adam and Eve were cast out for sin, is called this.

clue.text: Trader upset by delay

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A merchant is annoyed by a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to hold it back or slow it down, a verb meaning delay.

clue.text: Lean over the counter where your shoes are repaired

parts.note: a ship heels when it leans over to one side
a bar is a counter across which drinks or services are served

explanation.surface: Someone leans across a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A heel bar is a British high-street booth for quick shoe repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small shop or counter offering quick shoe repairs while you wait.
